items.prompt: You delete 30 from this order-3 B-tree. What does it look like afterwards?
hints: Is 30 in a leaf or an internal node?
After removing a key from a leaf, check it still has the minimum, ⌈m/2⌉ − 1 = 1 key for order 3.
[28 | 30] becomes [28], which still has 1 key, so nothing else changes.

options.feedback: Right. The leaf still has the minimum number of keys, so the deletion is done.
Borrowing is only needed when a node drops below the minimum. [28] still has 1 key.
Merging is only needed when a node underflows and no sibling can spare a key.

items.prompt: You delete 20 from this order-3 B-tree, using the predecessor. Which key takes 20's place in the root?
hints: 20 is in an internal node, so it is replaced rather than removed.
The predecessor is the largest key in the left subtree.
Go left to [8 | 12]; the largest key there is 12. 12 moves up and the leaf becomes [8].

options.feedback: Yes. 12 is the largest key smaller than 20, so the order still holds.
28 is the successor. That method also works, but this question uses the predecessor.
8 is the smallest key on the left. The predecessor is the largest.

items.prompt: You delete 8 from this order-3 B-tree. What does it look like afterwards?
hints: Removing 8 empties the left leaf. Can a sibling spare a key?
Borrow through the parent: the separator comes down, and the sibling's nearest key goes up.
The right sibling [28 | 30] can spare one: 20 comes down, 28 goes up. Result: [28] over [20] and [30].

options.feedback: Right. The key passes through the parent, so every key stays in its range.
28 cannot move straight across: it would sit left of 20 while being larger than 20.
Merge only when no sibling can spare a key. Here the right sibling can.
An empty leaf breaks the minimum-keys rule. The underflow must be fixed.

items.prompt: You delete 8 from this order-3 B-tree. What happens to its height?
hints: Removing 8 empties the left leaf. Can its sibling spare a key?
If no sibling can spare a key, merge with one and pull the separator down.
The leaf, 20 and [30] merge into [20 | 30]. The root is now empty, so [20 | 30] becomes the root: one level shorter.

options.text: It shrinks by one level: [20 | 30] becomes the root
options.feedback: Yes. A B-tree only gets shorter at the root, so all leaves stay level.

options.text: It stays the same: 30 moves into the empty leaf
options.feedback: Then 30 would sit left of 20 while being larger, and the right leaf would be empty.

options.text: It stays the same, with an empty leaf on the left
options.feedback: An empty leaf breaks the minimum-keys rule. The underflow must be fixed.

items.prompt: Someone deleted a key from an order-5 B-tree and drew this. Is it a valid order-5 B-tree?
hints: Count the keys in each non-root node.
In order 5, every node except the root needs at least 2 keys.
[10] underflowed and was not fixed. It should have borrowed from [30 | 40 | 50].
